controls.name: Session bound to its agent
controls.description: An agent can act only inside an AgentSession created for that same agent. A session id copied by another agent is refused.

controls.name: Agent lifecycle state
controls.description: Only an active agent can act or be given a new session. Quarantined and suspended agents are refused everywhere at once (the kill switch).

controls.name: Session validity
controls.description: A session must be active and unexpired. Closing or revoking a session stops the agent immediately.

controls.name: Human actor still active
controls.description: An agent session dies with the human behind it. Deprovisioning a person stops every agent acting on their behalf.

controls.name: Delegation within the human's entitlements
controls.description: A human can delegate to an agent only capabilities the human holds and the use case permits. The agent never inherits the human's whole privilege set.

controls.name: Session tier ceiling
controls.description: A session's tier ceiling is at most the human's clearance, the use case ceiling and the agent's clearance, whichever is lowest.

controls.name: Agent registered for the use case
controls.description: A use case names the agents that may run it. No session starts for any other agent.

controls.name: Effective capability intersection
controls.description: An agent may use a capability only if it was delegated in this session AND organization policy permits it for the use case. Everything else is denied by default.

controls.name: Fail closed
controls.description: Any error while building or evaluating a decision (unknown entity, schema mismatch, evaluation error) is a deny, never a skipped check.

controls.name: Request integrity
controls.description: The capability the Gateway checks is the action the connector will execute; a request where they disagree is refused.

controls.name: Resource tier ceiling
controls.description: An agent cannot touch a resource labelled above its session's tier ceiling, even when the human behind it could.

controls.name: No write-down
controls.description: Once a session has read data at a tier, it cannot write or send to a destination labelled lower, such as an external mailbox. Hijacked instructions cannot move data out.

controls.name: Model clearance
controls.description: Data goes only to models cleared for its tier. A session holding confidential data cannot call a model cleared for internal.

controls.name: Labelled memory
controls.description: Every memory entry carries the tier and provenance of the session that wrote it, and is returned to agents as labelled data, never as instructions.

controls.name: Labelled tool output
controls.description: Every tool result comes back labelled with the tier and origin of what it contains. Reading it raises the session's taint, and content from outside the organization marks the session as having untrusted input.

controls.name: Untrusted input gates high-impact actions
controls.description: After a session has ingested content from outside its trust boundary (an inbound ticket, another agent's message), any high-impact action needs a human approval.

controls.name: File intake and release
controls.description: A file enters or leaves an agent's workspace only through a Gateway scan. Its type comes from its bytes; executables, archives, the EICAR test signature, files with no text to scan and files carrying card numbers, IBANs, PESEL numbers or keys are refused. An accepted upload is catalogued with its tier before the agent can read it.

controls.name: Input content filter
controls.description: What a person types to an agent is checked before any model sees it. Payment card numbers, IBANs, PESEL numbers, API keys, private keys and names of resources above the session ceiling are refused, and the message stays with the person.

controls.name: Redaction by sensitivity profile
controls.description: Personal data that a use case may handle but a model should not see is replaced with [REDACTED:<CLASS>] before the message reaches the agent. Each use case runs under a strictness profile (strict, balanced, permissive) that says, per detector, block, redact or record.

controls.name: Output content filter
controls.description: What a model or a tool returns is checked before the agent gets it. Card numbers, IBANs, PESEL numbers, keys, email addresses and phone numbers are redacted or the result is withheld, per the use case's profile; known exfiltration constructs such as data-carrying markdown images are removed.

controls.name: Semantic injection classifier
controls.description: An injection and jailbreak classifier trained on Polish and English attacks runs inside the Gateway on every message, every action's data and every tool result. It reads through leetspeak, spaced letters, homoglyphs and base64, and explains which words drove its score. Its score is compared with the profile's adherence thresholds.

controls.name: Known-exploit signatures
controls.description: Requests, messages, files and model artifacts are matched against signatures of exploits that worked against AI infrastructure and agents (ShadowRay, Probllama, Langflow code validation, Log4Shell, metadata-service SSRF, EchoLeak-style image exfiltration, MCP tool poisoning). A blocking signature denies; a reviewing one needs a person.

controls.name: Unsafe deserialization and model code execution
controls.description: Pickles, PyTorch checkpoints, NumPy object arrays, Keras models and GGUF files are opened without being loaded. A pickle that imports something able to run commands, a Keras Lambda layer, or a GGUF chat template that reaches Python internals is refused.

controls.name: Model supply chain
controls.description: An agent may bring a model in from a public hub only pinned to a full commit hash, from a trusted publisher, without running repository code, and in a format that cannot execute on load. Publisher names one or two letters away from a trusted one are refused as typosquats; repositories on the threat feed are refused.

controls.name: Model allowlist
controls.description: Agents call only models the organization has listed, and a listed model can be switched off without touching any agent. A model that is not listed or not enabled is refused before a token is spent.

controls.name: Token budget and cost accounting
controls.description: Every session has a token budget next to its spending budget. A model call reserves its worst case (prompt plus output cap) before it runs and is charged what it actually used, priced per token for external models and per second of compute for local ones.

controls.name: Live configuration with last-good fallback
controls.description: Policies, the controls catalog, guardrail profiles, budgets, the classifier and the signature baseline reload within about a second of a change, without a restart. A change that does not validate is rejected and the previous configuration keeps running; both outcomes are security events.

controls.name: Pinned MCP tool descriptors
controls.description: Each MCP tool is pinned to the hash of its reviewed descriptor. A changed description or schema blocks the tool before any agent sees it, until an admin reviews and re-pins it.

parameters.pinnedDescriptorHash: sha256 of the reviewed payments descriptor

controls.name: Command templates
controls.description: shell.exec runs only commands that parse into an approved template with validated arguments. Pipes, substitutions and downloads-to-shell never match.

controls.name: Delegated execution
controls.description: An agent runtime that executes its own tools (Claude Code) asks the Gateway before every tool call and executes only after allow. Each call maps to a capability; network egress and unmapped tools are denied, and an unreachable Gateway means deny.

controls.name: Mediated agent channel
controls.description: Agents talk only through the Gateway, only to peers their use case names, and only to active agents. Each message records sender, receiver, use case, capability, provenance and trace id.

controls.name: Receiver clearance
controls.description: An agent cannot pass data to another agent cleared for a lower tier than the data it holds.

controls.name: A message is not a delegation
controls.description: An agent cannot ask another agent to perform a capability it does not hold itself. Received messages mark the receiver's session as having untrusted input.

controls.name: Approval required by use case
controls.description: Capabilities the use case lists need a human approval of the exact action before they run.

controls.name: Step-up required by use case
controls.description: Capabilities the use case lists need an approver who has just re-authenticated with OTP (acr level 2).

controls.name: Payment threshold
controls.description: A transfer above the use case threshold needs an approval with step-up. A transfer without an amount is refused.

controls.name: Approval evidence from the Gateway
controls.description: The approval card shows the exact parameters, resource, tier and provenance as the Gateway resolved them. Text written by the agent is shown only as labelled agent-supplied text.

controls.name: Session budget
controls.description: Each session has a spending budget; an action that would exceed it is refused. Action prices and the session budgets per use case come from guardrails.yaml.

controls.name: Rate limit
controls.description: A use case caps how many actions an agent may take per minute; a burst beyond it is refused.

controls.name: Circuit breaker
controls.description: Repeated denials from one agent within a short window trip a breaker that quarantines the agent, stopping a cascade before it spreads.

controls.name: Suspend high-impact capabilities
controls.description: During an incident, high-impact capabilities (payments, outbound email, shell) can be suspended for a whole team or a single agent in one step.

controls.name: AI analysis only tightens
controls.description: Semantic analysis (the in-Gateway classifier, optionally with an LLM judge) can turn allow into require_approval or deny. It never sees a deterministic deny as negotiable and can never loosen a decision.

controls.name: Every decision is a trace
controls.description: Each action is recorded with who initiated it, which agent, why, what capability, which resource, which policies and controls decided, and every pipeline stage as a span.
